item.description:
This is my first release (as Kim)

Lyric Language: Indonesian
Genre: Pop, Rock
Style: Sophisti-pop, Art Pop, Soft Rock
Year: Song 1990, music video: 1994

"Yogyakarta" is a legendary song by Indonesian pop-rock band KLa Project, from their second studio album, Kedua, released in 1990. Produced by the band itself, the song features Katon Bagaskara (as Vocal), Adi Adrian (as Keyboardist), and Romulo "Lilo" Radjadin's (as Guitarist). Although now known as a song about a city in Central Java, its original inspiration came from European cities, specifically Spain.

The song was originally planned to have a Spanish or European theme because the KLa Project members had just returned from a trip there. This is reflected in the musical elements, which use castanets—a typical Spanish percussion instrument. However, because musician Fariz RM had already released the hit song "Barcelona," the band decided to change direction to avoid being perceived as copycats. Katon Bagaskara surprisingly completed the lyrics for this song just an hour before the vocal recording process began, amidst deadline pressure. He reportedly even finished writing them in the studio restroom.

The name "Yogyakarta" was ultimately chosen because it was deemed to rhyme well with the existing melody. Interestingly, the word "Jogja" is only mentioned once in the lyrics—a specific request from Katon Bagaskara's mother to ensure the city's name remains prominent in the song's identity. Musically, "Yogyakarta" has been described as the pinnacle of the Indonesian sophisti-pop genre, with Katon's poetic lyrics acting as a counterpoint to the beauty of the melody composed by Adi and Lilo.

Musically, "Yogyakarta" is characterized by its lush, atmospheric production. It opens with a distinctive, reverb-heavy synthesizer melody composed by Adi Adrian, which sets a nostalgic and slightly melancholic tone. This is complemented by Lilo’s clean, melodic guitar riffs and Katon’s smooth, baritone vocals. Critics have described the song as a "sonic painting," noting its use of layered textures and a sophisticated harmonic structure that was considered avant-garde for the Indonesian pop scene at the time. The arrangement successfully blends Western pop-rock sensibilities with a distinctly Indonesian soul, avoiding traditional folk instruments while still "sounding" inherently local.

Upon its release, "Yogyakarta" became an immediate critical darling and a massive commercial success. It dominated the airwaves and helped the album Kedua achieve multi-platinum status. The song swept the 1991 BASF Awards—the most prestigious music honors in Indonesia during that era—winning in several major categories, including Best Pop Song and Best Arrangement.

In 2009, Rolling Stone Indonesia ranked "Yogyakarta" at number 16 on its list of the "150 Best Indonesian Songs of All Time." The magazine praised the song for its lyrical depth and its role in elevating the standards of Indonesian pop production. It remains a staple of Indonesian radio and is frequently cited by musicologists as one of the most perfectly crafted songs in the nation's history.

While the song was released in 1990, it's most iconic music video was the 1994 version directed by Igor Tamerlan.
The song’s music video is equally iconic, featuring the trio in various historic and cultural settings around the city, such as the Malioboro district and the Sultan’s Palace (Kraton). Filmed with a soft-focus, cinematic lens, the video reinforced the song's themes of nostalgia and timelessness. Tamerlan’s direction helped reinforce the song’s themes of nostalgia and timelessness, cementing the visual identity of the track for a generation of fans.

A significant milestone in the song’s history occurred in 1996, when KLa Project performed a stripped-back, acoustic version for their live album KLakustik. Recorded at Gedung Kesenian Jakarta, this version featured a more prominent piano arrangement and became arguably as famous as the original studio recording, proving the song's versatility across different musical formats.

Over the decades, "Yogyakarta" has evolved into more than just a hit single; it has become the unofficial national anthem for the city of Yogyakarta itself. It is a cultural touchstone for the Indonesian diaspora, often used in tourism campaigns and played during official provincial ceremonies. The song’s enduring popularity lies in its universal theme of "longing for home," making it a resonant piece for anyone who has experienced the bittersweet feeling of nostalgia.

To this day, "Yogyakarta" is the closing highlight of every KLa Project concert, often performed with the audience singing every word in unison. It has been covered by numerous artists across various genres, from jazz to keroncong, yet the original 1990 recording remains the definitive version that captured the heart of a nation.
